2M.5 Praise should be offered to God continually.

precepts.text: Thou lovest righteousness and hatest wickedness, therefore God hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness. Hearken, O daughter, forget thine own people and thy father's house; so shall the king greatly desire thy beauty, for he is thy Lord, and worship thou him. Like a marriage, the Lord will not share us; love righteousness, hate iniquity, and he desires our beauty as he created it.
precepts.point: I will surely avenge them; my people is led as a flock to the slaughter; I will not suffer them now to dwell in the land of Egypt, but bring them out with a mighty hand and smite Egypt with plagues as before and destroy all the land thereof. As before means a coming Egypt, the United States. When it comes, we do not want to go down with it.
precepts.why:
The beauty of Israel was cast down because we left our God, so now we have to return. David shows how: “Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” We have to love righteousness and hate iniquity.

“All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces”, and “upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir.”

“Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house”. The Lord says listen up. Just like a marriage, sisters, you have to focus on your lord. The Lord does not want to share us with anybody else; he wants us to focus on him and him only.

“So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him.” When we get ourselves right, turn back to the Lord, love righteousness and hate iniquity, he will desire our beauty, the way he created it. And we worship him and him only, not the beauty of Egypt.

precepts.text: Judah is a lion's whelp; the scepter shall not depart from Judah until Shiloh come, and to Him shall the gathering of the people be.
precepts.point: That rulership belongs to Christ from the tribe of Judah, and if we keep the commandments we will be heirs with Him in the kingdom.

note.label: Psalm 45: Thy Throne, O God, Is Forever

precepts.why:
“Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre.” Whose sceptre is that? Jacob told Judah: “Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father’s children shall bow down before thee. Judah is a lion’s whelp”. And: “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.”

That rulership belongs to Christ from the tribe of Judah. The sceptre stays with Judah until Shiloh come, and to him the people are gathered. If we keep the commandments, we will be heirs with him in the kingdom whose sceptre is a right sceptre.

precepts.text: To the Son He says thy throne is forever and ever, a scepter of righteousness is the scepter of thy kingdom.
precepts.point: That rulership belongs to Christ from the tribe of Judah, and if we keep the commandments we will be heirs with Him in the kingdom.

note.label: Psalm 45: Thy Throne, O God, Is Forever

precepts.why:
Hebrews shows exactly who Psalm 45:6 is spoken to. Of the Son the Father said, “Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee”, and “when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him.” “And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire. But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.”

So the throne that is for ever and ever, and the right sceptre, belong to the Son, Christ from the tribe of Judah. The sceptre of righteousness is the right sceptre, and if we keep the commandments we will be heirs with him in that kingdom.

precepts.text: The married woman cares how she may please her husband, being gone from her father's house.
precepts.point: This is the woman leaving her father's house for her husband's house when we live righteously; she now cares to please her husband.

note.label: Psalm 45: Thy Throne, O God, Is Forever

precepts.why:
“Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house; So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty”. This is the woman leaving her father's house for her husband's house. Corinthians shows the change: “There is difference also between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman careth for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit: but she that is married careth for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.”

Gone from her father's house, the married woman now cares how she may please her husband, and that is when the king greatly desires her beauty, when we live righteously. “for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him.”

precepts.text: These are the statutes between a man and his wife, and between the father and his daughter yet in her youth in her father's house.
precepts.point: This is the woman leaving her father's house for her husband's house when we live righteously; she now cares to please her husband.

note.label: Psalm 45: Thy Throne, O God, Is Forever

precepts.why:
The daughter is told to “forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house”. Numbers shows the two houses a woman belongs to: “These are the statutes, which the Lord commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, between the father and his daughter, being yet in her youth in her father’s house.”

Yet in her youth she is in her father's house, under her father; then she is a wife, under her husband. That is the move Psalm 45 speaks of: the woman leaving her father's house for her husband's house when we live righteously, so that she now cares to please her husband, and “he is thy Lord; and worship thou him.”

precepts.text: Whosoever does the will of the Father is His brother, sister, and mother, above the ties of one's own people.
precepts.point: This is the woman leaving her father's house for her husband's house when we live righteously; she now cares to please her husband.

note.label: Psalm 45: Thy Throne, O God, Is Forever

precepts.why:
“forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house”. Christ showed what stands above the ties of one's own people. When told “thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to speak with thee”, he answered, “Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?” and stretched forth his hand toward his disciples: “Behold my mother and my brethren! For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.”

Whosoever does the will of the Father is his brother, sister and mother, above one's own people and father's house. So the daughter who hearkens, forgets her own people and worships her Lord is doing the will of the Father, and the king greatly desires her beauty.
